20021127-1.c.citation: declare-call-define of `llabs` (§7.24.6.1): the file declares `long long llabs (long long);`, calls `llabs(-1)`, and defines `long long llabs (long long b) { abort (); }`. It passes only under builtin recognition, which is a compiler optimisation and not a rule of C. Modelling the <stdlib.h> builtins by name to satisfy it would adopt GCC's optimiser behaviour as if it were C semantics.
